findings.detail: This PR introduces the first early-return path in `runLookup` and correctly restores `setStatus(ProcessingStatus.IDLE)` on it (line 219). That makes the surrounding gap more visible: `readGrid` (201-202) and `buildLookup` (205) are unguarded, and the function has no `try`/`finally`. If either throws on a malformed sheet, `status` stays `ProcessingStatus.PROCESSING` forever, so the Run button (line 469, `disabled={status === ProcessingStatus.PROCESSING}`) is permanently disabled and the tab is unusable until the user hits Reset — with no error surfaced. `handleDownload` (295-299) already has exactly this shape and gets it right. This is pre-existing code the diff does not add, which is why it is `low` rather than `medium`; what would raise it is a confirmed throwing input in `readGrid`/`buildLookup` for a realistic sheet.
findings.summary: runLookup has no try/catch — a throw leaves the tab stuck in PROCESSING

findings.detail: `addLog("Settings changed during the lookup — run it again.", 'warning')` is the only user-visible output of the new supersede path, and it is a bare English literal while the rest of this component's UI strings come from `t.smartLookup.*` (`TRANSLATIONS[language]`). The app ships a full Arabic layer and sets `dir="rtl"` (App.tsx:222), so an Arabic user who trips this path gets an untranslated string as the only explanation for why their results vanished. Noted as `info` rather than `low` because every other `addLog` call in this file (lines 186, 239, 293) is already English — this is consistent with its surroundings, not a regression.
findings.summary: New user-facing log message is hardcoded English in a bilingual app
